step_by_step_reasoning: The user presents an architecture from the 'This is My Architecture' video featuring Fiverr's PCI DSS Level 1 compliant payment processing system. The original traditional architecture (with EC2 load balancers, app servers, antivirus, bastion hosts, databases, and HSM) was simplified using native AWS serverless and security services. Visual inspection and transcript details confirm the active components: Application Load Balancer (ALB) routes traffic to Fargate container app servers. Fargate fetches sensitive parameters and API tokens from Systems Manager (SSM) Parameter Store, which uses KMS for encryption/decryption. Continuous security monitoring and audit logging are handled by GuardDuty and CloudTrail.

graph.name: Fiverr PCI DSS Compliant Payment Architecture
graph.notes: Fiverr simplified its PCI DSS Level 1 architecture by replacing self-managed servers and security tooling with serverless compute (Fargate), managed load balancing (ALB), parameter encryption (SSM and KMS), and automated threat monitoring (GuardDuty and CloudTrail).

nodes.name: ALB

nodes.name: Fargate
nodes.notes: Runs serverless containerized payment applications without requiring EC2 instance management

nodes.name: SSM Parameter Store
nodes.notes: Stores configuration data, API endpoints, and sensitive credentials

nodes.name: KMS
nodes.notes: Provides encryption and decryption keys for parameters stored in SSM

nodes.name: GuardDuty
nodes.notes: Provides intelligent threat detection and security monitoring for PCI compliance

nodes.name: CloudTrail
nodes.notes: Captures operational API activity and audit logs for PCI DSS compliance

edges.notes: ALB routes payment requests to Fargate application containers
Fargate requests configuration and secret parameters from SSM Parameter Store
SSM Parameter Store uses KMS keys to decrypt sensitive secrets for Fargate
API calls and administrative activity are recorded in CloudTrail
Container activity and network security events are monitored by GuardDuty
